transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-16
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood SE), Victor (CTO, Celestia), Rina (Backend), Samir (SRE), Aisha (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
- Goal: Walk through Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching and KV/prefix caching to reduce token unit cost while keeping P95 latency under 220ms for primary endpoints.
- Focus: prefetch/lookahead window, cache TTL/eviction, batch sizing and steady-state concurrency, sample cost simulation for 5M monthly queries.
- Next steps: run sandbox benchmark, share cost spreadsheet, provide traffic traces.

Topics: cost sim assumptions, cache hit rate sensitivity, prefetch window tradeoffs, session affinity, private deployment considerations (VPC/KMS).

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick roll call — we got Victor, Rina, Samir from Celestia, and Aisha, and from our side it's me, Maya and Liam. sound good?
[00:12] Victor: yep all good, and sorry in advance I might duck out at 15:45 for another call.
[00:16] Maya: no worries, we'll prioritize the cost sim and the benchmark details before then.
[00:23] Jordan: cool, objective today is to walk the Optimize console recommendations — specifically batching and prefix / KV cache prefetch — and run through a sample savings model on your traffic profile. we sent a short spreadsheet earlier, but we'll flesh it out live.
[00:38] Rina: great, high level we have about 5M completions a month across two endpoints: short chat replies (avg 75 tokens) and doc-qa (avg 320 tokens). latency SLO is 220ms P95 for chat; doc-qa can be 600ms P95. data residency in EU, SOC2 required, and we're evaluating hosted vs dedicated; private is a later option.
[01:05] Maya: thanks, that's helpful. a few clarifying q's: are you sessionizing users (session affinity) today? and what's your 95th percentile concurrency?
[01:14] Samir: we do light session affinity — cookies carry a session id — concurrency peaks ~180 qps across both endpoints, but average steady is ~40 qps.
[01:24] Liam: perfect. those numbers make both batching and prefix cache high-leverage. we'll show two sims: aggressive prefix prefetch (lookahead 48 tokens) and conservative (lookahead 8).

[02:10] Jordan: first, quick primer: prefix/KV cache stores model KV states for repeated prefixes so doc-qa and multi-turn chat get speedups and lower token compute. prefetch means populating likely future KV entries proactively for active sessions. tradeoff: prefetch increases memory and some GPU cycles (writes) but reduces token-decoding compute and latency for hits.
[02:34] Rina: sounds right — is prefetch supported in hosted mode or only dedicated/private?
[02:39] Maya: supported in hosted, though dedicated gives more control over cache capacity and TTLs. private deployments can integrate with KMS/HSM for key management if you need it.

[03:05] Victor: show us the numbers — we've had internal estimates but they're all over the place.
[03:09] Jordan: ok jumping into the cost sim: baseline assumptions we used for this call (please verify): model = 13B open variant quantized, cost-of-inference per token on hosted = $0.00012 per 1k prompt tokens (example), 1k response tokens = $0.0009 (these placeholders will be updated when we run your trace). hit rate sensitivity: 10%, 35%, 60% scenarios.
[03:41] Samir: that prompt/response split looks low for our numbers, can we plug your higher-cost peak numbers later?
[03:45] Maya: absolutely — that's why we want your traces; we'll re-run with your per-region pricing and observed seq lengths.

[04:10] Liam: demo time — Optimize console, savings simulator. (screen share audio) top-left is the scenario selector: concurrency, batch size target, prefix prefetch window, cache TTL, and assumed hit rate. we start with baseline: no prefetch, batch target 8, concurrency 40 qps.
[04:33] Jordan: note about batching: for chat with short replies, too-large batches can raise latency; our runtime does continuous batching but we recommend a per-route max batch size that maps to your P95 latency budget. e.g., batch=6 for chat gave P95 ~190ms in our sim, batch=12 pushed P95 above 260ms.
[04:55] Rina: is that with warm KV cache or cold start?
[04:58] Maya: sim assumes steady-state warm cache when we report optimized latency; cold starts are a different column in the sheet.

[05:30] Jordan: now the prefetch options: lookahead window (how many tokens of subsequent decoding we precompute) — small window (8 tokens) gives modest hit rate lift at low memory cost; large window (48 tokens) needs more cache entries but can push hit rate from 35% to 60% for doc-qa patterns where user reads sequential paragraphs.
[05:51] Victor: any rule of thumb for TTL/eviction? our sessions are often inactive for minutes.
[05:55] Maya: TTL + LRU eviction — we typically suggest keeping TTL equal to expected session inactivity window. for Celestia, with session affinity and average session length 4m, TTL 6 minutes is a reasonable start. you can tune upward for higher hit rates.

[06:20] Rina: and memory usage? how much more RAM on the GPU for 48-token lookahead?
[06:26] Liam: rough back-of-envelope: each KV entry is proportional to hidden-state size; for a 13B model ~1.1MB per 1k tokens of KV. 48-token lookahead per active session x 10k active sessions would be ~~528MB. these are approximate but give ordering.
[06:51] Samir: ok that's manageable.

[07:15] Jordan: switching back to cost sim. with your 5M monthly completions split (80% chat, 20% doc-qa), baseline monthly inference cost (no prefetch, batch6) = $12,800 (placeholder). with lookahead 48 and batch tuned (chat batch 6, doc-qa batch 16) and assumed 55% hit rate for doc-qa and 30% for chat, simulated cost drops ~28% to $9,200.
[07:47] Victor: 28% is significant — does that account for extra prefetch write cycles?
[07:52] Maya: yes the sim includes additional write ops and memory overhead; the net is still savings because decoding compute per token is more expensive than the prefetch overhead.

[08:20] Rina: can Redwood Optimize recommend per-route configs automatically? or we have to tune manually?
[08:25] Maya: Optimize offers recommendations: it looks at token length histograms, sequence patterns and suggests batch targets, lookahead size, and TTLs. you can accept suggestions or run sandbox simulations first.

[09:00] Jordan: quick detour — private deployment notes: if you go private/VPC, you'll get more control over placement and you can ensure that KV cache memory is persistent within your cluster; also KMS/HSM integration for key rotation. that affects operational costs but not the per-token compute numbers dramatically.
[09:22] Victor: since we have EU residency needs, private might be attractive but the timeline to production matters. what's typical onboard time for private?
[09:28] Liam: For mid-market customers, 6-12 weeks with infra templates; dedicated is faster (2-4 weeks) and hosted is immediate.

[10:05] Jordan: returning to tradeoffs — we also model fallback policies: if cache miss spikes or we lose a node, Redwood's smart routing can fail over to a smaller model variant to preserve latency and limit cost. that was requested by a couple of your product folks earlier in the questionnaire.
[10:20] Aisha: yes that fallback idea is attractive — preserves UX during partial outages.

[11:00] (Screen share continues) Maya: demoing the scenario where we throttle prefetch during peak to keep memory stable. Console shows a heatmap: hit rate vs concurrency; you can set policy rules for region-level prefetch disable when memory pressure > 80%.
[11:37] Rina: nice, can we tie those rules to alerts in our PagerDuty?
[11:40] Liam: yes, there's alert hooks and webhooks; we can forward metrics and trigger PD.

[12:05] Victor: let's talk real numbers you need from us to make the sim accurate.
[12:09] Jordan: ideal: 7-day token length histogram, sample 1% of requests with session ids, endpoints mapping, and your current cost per GPU-hour if you have it. also any expected traffic growth next 3 months.
[12:22] Victor: we can get that by Friday.

[13:00] Samir: on the SRE side, what are recommended CPU/GPU reservations per instance? we run in k8s.
[13:06] Maya: for the 13B quantized, we recommend 1 GPU + 4 vCPU for serving process and warming. bursting capacity should be set to 20% of baseline to avoid cold starts.

[14:00] Jordan: another point — batching strategy differences for chat vs doc-qa. chat needs low-max-batch-size with short timeouts; doc-qa can tolerate larger batches and longer latency. Optimize supports per-route and per-model config.

[15:10] Victor: quick clarification — you mentioned sessionization. we tie session ids to a single worker currently; will that reduce batching efficiency?
[15:19] Maya: it can. session affinity increases cache hit rates but may reduce global batching opportunities. we often recommend a hybrid: session affinity for KV locality but allow batch pooling across a small set of workers to get batching benefits. that's a config in the router.

[16:00] (Victor leaves for a brief call)
[16:05] Jordan: we'll keep going — one more demo slide: sensitivity chart. this plots end-to-end cost vs hit rate for different lookahead sizes. interestingly, marginal benefit from 40%->60% hit for doc-qa is much higher than 60%->75% because of diminishing returns as you saturate GPU memory.
[16:40] Rina: can Optimize recommend a lookahead per-model?
[16:44] Liam: yes, it suggests lookahead per workload based on your sequence patterns and memory budget. there is also a conservative mode that tries to minimize memory delta.

[17:30] Samir: about security: you mentioned audit logs and token-level tracing. do we get access to raw prompts in hosted?
[17:37] Jordan: hosted redwood keeps prompts encrypted at rest; audit logs include hashes unless you opt-in. for enterprise, private deploy gives full control and local logging. SOC2 report is available to customers under NDA.

[18:10] Rina: latency numbers again: can you guarantee P95 220ms for chat with prefetch?
[18:15] Maya: guarantees come with dedicated/reserved capacity SLAs. hosted can hit that in many cases but if strict SLA is required we recommend dedicated with pinned instances.

[19:00] Jordan: quick walkthrough of how to accept Optimize suggestions: one-click apply to staging route, console runs a dry-run and simulates 24-hour forecast. apply to prod after sandbox verification.
[19:24] Rina: what's the rollback story?
[19:27] Liam: built-in canary and automatic rollback on error or latency regressions; you set thresholds.

[20:00] (Demo pauses, questions)
[20:12] Aisha: for product, what's typical UX improvement from reduced latency — any numbers?
[20:17] Jordan: customers often see improvement in engagement metrics: e.g., reply rate +3–7% when chat latency drops from 350ms to 180ms. depends on product.

[21:00] Maya: we should run a quick micro-benchmark on your dev trace in the sandbox to show expected P95 and cost delta; that gives credible numbers for your finance team.
[21:10] Victor (rejoins): I'm back, sorry — sounds like you covered the important parts.
[21:15] Jordan: no prob. recap: we'll run a sandbox sim with your traces, share a cost spreadsheet and recommendation set (batch sizes, lookahead, TTLs), and schedule a 2-hour hands-on sandbox session.

[22:00] Rina: one last operational question — cache invalidation when user updates docs, can we evict KV for that session?
[22:07] Liam: yes there are APIs to evict per-session or per-prefix; you can integrate invalidation into your doc update pipeline.

[23:00] Jordan: ok let's capture action items. (reads) Jordan to send cost sim by Thursday; Maya to run benchmark; Victor to provide traces. schedule sandbox.

[23:30] (Wrap up)
[23:45] Samir: thanks, this was useful. we'll get the traces and target next steps.
[24:00] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the spreadsheet.

Notes on transcription quality: some product names and acronyms may be mis-transcribed (K V cache -> K-V cash, lookahead sometimes as 'look head') and numbers are placeholders until we run your actual traces.

End of transcript.
